title: Multimodal learning evaluates vertebroplasty cement-leakage risk
summary: Six learned classifiers combined clinical, conventional CT and radiomic features to evaluate cement leakage after vertebroplasty. Development used 378 patients, with additional external and later-acquired validation cohorts of 45 and 50 patients. Patient grouping was retained during splits and tuning. Because injected cement volume is a predictor, this is a perioperative risk analysis rather than a purely preoperative forecast; treatment benefit was not tested.
ai_technology: XGBoost; random forest; support vector machine; learned classifiers

source_review.scope: Primary relevant Methods/results/limitations and exact front/canonical identity; current primary PubMed linked correction/retraction metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Patient-grouped training/tuning, internal testing and unchanged-model application to external and later-acquired cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Prospectively timed predictions before outcome ascertainment and benefit from model-guided injection planning remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers integrate clinical, CT and selected radiomic variables to estimate perioperative cement-leakage probability.
